title: A section and its normal bundle
statement:
Work in the finite-coefficient purity setting [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, uniformizer $\ell$, and $n\ge1$, so $\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Use the small pro-etale sites and $D^b_{ctf}$ of these conventions, the derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; put $\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda$.

Let $S,V$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $g:V\to S$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $s:S\to V$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $g\circ s=\operatorname{id}_S$. Then $s$ is a regular immersion of codimension $d$: near every point of $s(S)$ its defining ideal has a regular generating sequence of length $d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], with the empty sequence allowed when $d=0$. Let $N_s$ be its normal bundle [def-pur-normal-bundle], with projection $\pi:N_s\to S$ and zero section $z:S\to N_s$.

The deformation to the normal bundle [def-pur-dnc-section-family] is
$$
\operatorname{Def}_s(V)=\operatorname{Bl}_{s(S)\times\{0\}}(V\times_S\mathbf A^1_S)\setminus\widetilde{V\times_S\{0\}},
$$
where the removed subscheme is the strict transform. It has a smooth morphism of pure relative dimension $d$, $\widetilde g:\operatorname{Def}_s(V)\to\mathbf A^1_S$, and a closed section $\widetilde s$. Its pairs over $t=1$ and $t=0$ are $(g,s)$ and $(\pi,z)$. Etale coordinates of the pair near the section give deformation coordinates $u_i$ with $x_i=tu_i$; at $t=0$ these are linear coordinates on $N_s$. This is a statement about etale charts near the section, without requiring $V$ itself to be an affine space.

Write $a:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ and $i_0,i_1:S\to\mathbf A^1_S$ for the sections $t=0,1$. Put
$$
F=L\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g},\qquad C=Ls^*\omega_g
$$
as in [def-pur-section-invariant]. There is a unique isomorphism
$$
\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\sim}La^*C
$$
whose pullback by $i_1$ is the identity of $C$ under the canonical fibre identification $Li_1^*F\simeq C$ and $Li_1^*La^*C\simeq C$. The inverse of its restriction at zero is the canonical isomorphism
$$
Ls^*\omega_g\xrightarrow{\sim}Lz^*\omega_\pi
\quad\text{in }D^b_{ctf}(S_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z).
$$
The family $F$ and $C$ are shifts by $[2d]$ of finite locally constant rank-one $\Lambda$-sheaves [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Etale coordinates show locally on $S$ that $F$ is pulled back from $S$; no assertion that every locally constant sheaf on $\mathbf A^1_S$ is so pulled back is made. Both $\kappa$ and the displayed fibre isomorphism commute with etale localization and with every $k$-morphism $S'\to S$ from a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, without flatness or smoothness of that morphism.

proof.text: First check the domain of all exceptional operations. A field is Noetherian; $S,V$ and $V\times_S\mathbf A^1_S$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The affine-line projection is separated and finite type, since on affine charts it adjoins one generator and its diagonal is cut out by $t_1-t_2$. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], the product projection to $\mathbf A^1_S$ is separated finite type. The centre has ideal $(I,t)$ on $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$, where $I$ defines the original closed section; this ideal sheaf is quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and is finite type because the coordinate rings are Noetherian. Thus the blowup is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], hence separated finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its open deformation subscheme and its intersections with affine opens are Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The open inclusion is therefore quasi-compact, hence finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], and separated since its diagonal is an isomorphism. Separatedness and local finite type compose by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e); quasi-compactness composes using finite affine covers. This proves that the deformation and its morphism to $\mathbf A^1_S$ are separated finite type over the required bases. The vector bundle, after its construction below, is separated finite type by a finite cover of $S$ by trivial bundles: its affine charts have $d$ polynomial generators and closed diagonal. Consequently all instances of $R^!$ below are in the finite-type domain of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. To establish regularity before using a normal bundle, apply [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] around each section point, and shrink the base so the section factors through the source chart. Write $m$ for the number of coordinates initially supplied by the normal-form theorem. By [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], the standard projection $\mathbf A^m_{S_i}\to S_i$ is smooth of relative dimension $m$. The chart map is etale, hence smooth of relative dimension zero. Composition in [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2) makes its composite with the standard projection smooth of relative dimension $m$. The same permanence statement applied to the open chart inclusion and the restriction of $g$ makes that composite smooth of relative dimension $d$. At the chosen section point its fibre has a single well-defined local dimension, so $m=d$. Empty base charts may be discarded. Thus this chart has $d$ relative coordinates. Subtract their values along the section; translation is an automorphism of $\mathbf A^d$ and sends the section to zero. The etale map of the affine source neighborhood to $\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$ is separated: its diagonal is the base change of the source diagonal over $S_i$, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). The inverse image $P$ of the zero section is therefore separated etale over $S_i$, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and separated base change [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. The section into $P$ is open and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. Its complement in $P$ is closed in the source chart because $P$ is closed there, and can be removed. This gives etale coordinates of pairs with Cartesian square of centres, without presupposing the regularity or normal bundle of the section. At an image point the ideal is generated by $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ in an etale algebra over $R[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$. The latter variables form a regular sequence: after quotienting by their predecessors, multiplication by the next variable is injective by coefficient comparison. The local etale ring map is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to these successive injective multiplication maps. Their tensors identify with multiplication by $x_i$ on the corresponding quotient, so they remain injective. The final quotient is the nonzero local ring of the section. This proves the regular-sequence assertion, including the empty sequence when $d=0$. For clarity, its normal cone is the actual associated graded of [def-pur-normal-bundle]. On an affine coordinate chart write $A=R[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$, $T$ for the etale $A$-algebra, $J=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ and $I=JT$; the Cartesian centre gives $T/I=R$. Tensoring $J^{m+1}\subset J^m\subset A$ with the flat algebra $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identifies $I^m/I^{m+1}$ with $(J^m/J^{m+1})\otimes_A T$. The degree-$m$ monomials in the $X_i$ are an $R$-basis of $J^m/J^{m+1}$, by collecting polynomial coefficients. Since $J$ acts as zero, the tensor is its tensor over $R$ with $T/I=R$. Multiplication of monomials therefore identifies $\operatorname{gr}_I(T)$ with $R[U_1,\ldots,U_d]$ as a graded algebra. Thus the associated-graded spectrum is locally a rank-$d$ vector bundle, with zero section induced by its degree-zero augmentation; the linear degree-one transition maps give the normal bundle. When $d=0$, $I=0$ near the section, the graded algebra has only degree zero, and this cone is $S$ with projection and zero section both the identity. This verifies the rank-zero case directly without applying the positive-codimension convention of def-pur-regular-immersion. The deformation and family are the actual blowup-minus-strict-transform and pullback of [def-pur-dnc-section-family] and [def-pur-section-invariant]. Parts (1),(2),(4),(5) of [sk-lem-geometry] give the smooth deformation, its two pairs, the equation $x_i=tu_i$, and their base-change identifications; the deformed section is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion], applied to the separated deformation projection just verified. Put $\theta:Li_1^*F\simeq C$ and $\eta:Li_0^*F\simeq Lz^*\omega_\pi$ using part (1).

source.place: Local construction, coordinates and the two fibres; statement, regularity of the section

proof.text:
Choose the etale coordinate cover $\{S_i\to S\}$ in Step 1, with each $S_i$ affine of finite type over $S$. Such refinements are available by taking affine neighborhoods in the coordinate cover. Since $S$ is separated finite type over $k$, these cover members and their overlaps are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. The charts are neighborhoods of the section, with etale maps of pairs to $(\mathbf A^d_{S_i},0)$. Here is the induced etale map on deformation charts, rather than an identification of the source chart with affine space. Locally write $A=R[X_1,\ldots,X_d]\to T$ for this etale algebra and $J=(X_1,\ldots,X_d,t)\subset A[t]$. The algebra $T[t]$ is flat over $A[t]$: tensoring an $A[t]$-module with it is its tensor over $A$ with the flat module $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], $J^m\otimes_{A[t]}T[t]\to T[t]$ is injective with image $(JT[t])^m$ for every $m$. The degreewise identifications respect products, so the Rees algebra after this tensor is the Rees algebra of $JT[t]$. On the degree-zero localization at the homogeneous element $t$, they identify the deformation chart with
$$
\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(T\otimes_{R[X_1,\ldots,X_d]}R[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]\bigr),\qquad X_j\longmapsto tu_j.
$$
This is the $t$-chart of the blowup, i.e. the complement of the strict transform in the coordinate model of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](2),(4). Its map to $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]=\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}$ is a base change of $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. It contains the entire family section: the augmentation sends every $u_j$ to zero and $T$ to $T/(X_1,\ldots,X_d)=R$, with $t$ unchanged. Write $F_i,C_i$ for the restrictions. Here is the dualizing comparison used on these charts. By [lem-pur-co-smooth-etale-locality], an etale map $e$ is cohomologically smooth with $\omega_e\simeq\Lambda$. The smooth standard projection $p$ is cohomologically smooth: clauses (1),(2),(3) of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] give precisely the three conditions of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Thus [lem-pur-co-smooth-composition] gives $\omega_{pe}\simeq Le^*\omega_p$. Apply the same formula to the open inclusion of each chart into the original space; the section factors through that chart, so pulling back computes the original section invariant. The standard projection is a trivial rank-$d$ vector bundle, so [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] at $K=\Lambda$ yields isomorphisms $\alpha_i:F_i\simeq\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}(d)[2d]$ and $\beta_i:C_i\simeq\Lambda_{S_i}(d)[2d]$. Its base-change compatibility along $a_i$ identifies $La_i^*\Lambda_{S_i}(d)[2d]$ with $\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}(d)[2d]$. Arbitrary base change for the dualizing objects in [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](3) identifies all restrictions used here. This argument uses etale comparison near the sections, not an isomorphism of the whole pairs. All source charts here can be chosen affine, by restricting to principal affine opens in the base and their inverse images in an affine source chart. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), these etale maps are quasi-compact and of finite presentation, hence finite type. The open charts of the original and deformed spaces are Noetherian, so their inclusions are quasi-compact finite type by the open-subscheme and open-immersion statements used in Step 1. The charts and their overlaps are separated over $k$ by separated composition; every map between them is separated because its diagonal is the base change of the source diagonal over $k$, using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Hence the chartwise exceptional comparisons are all within the same finite-type formalism. On a principal source open $D(h)$, $(I^r)_h=(I_h)^r$ identifies the restricted Rees algebra and its blowup charts with the restricted deformation construction [def-pur-dnc-section-family]; thus these source charts contain the factored family section throughout the affine-line parameter.

source.place: Local construction: source-etale comparison and affine-space adjunction

proof.text: The finite-coefficient assertion of [prop-weil-twist-preserves] says that $\Lambda(d)$ is a finite locally constant rank-one sheaf. Thus the local models in Step 2 are sheaves in the common degree $r=-2d$. Apply [lem-pur-concentrated-complex-shift](2) to $F$ on the surjective etale cover $\coprod_i\mathbf A^1_{S_i}\to\mathbf A^1_S$, and to $C$ on $\coprod_i S_i\to S$. This lemma does not require the disjoint union to be of finite type. It gives concentration in degree $-2d$ and finite local constancy of $M_F=\mathcal H^{-2d}F$ and $M_C=\mathcal H^{-2d}C$. They have rank one, as checked on the cover in Step 2. Part (1) of the same lemma gives $F\simeq M_F[2d]$ and $C\simeq M_C[2d]$. Constant-coefficient inverse image is exact and is computed termwise by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], so these identifications also hold after every pullback below. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], removing the common shift identifies morphisms between these objects with ordinary module-sheaf morphisms, preserving equality and composition. Consequently the gluing below is gluing of morphisms of fixed sheaves.

source.place: Opening paragraph: shifts of lisse lines and reduction to sheaf morphisms

proof.text: Using the twist-pullback comparison of Step 2, set $\lambda_i=(La_i^*\beta_i)^{-1}\circ\alpha_i:F_i\simeq La_i^*C_i$. Let $\theta_i:Li_1^*F_i\simeq C_i$ be Step 1's fibre identification, put $h_i=(Li_1^*\lambda_i)\circ\theta_i^{-1}$, and define $\kappa_i=La_i^*(h_i^{-1})\circ\lambda_i$. Then $Li_1^*\kappa_i=h_i^{-1}\circ h_i\circ\theta_i=\theta_i$ since $a_i i_1=\operatorname{id}$. Every factor is invertible. This normalizes the comparison on every component, without choosing a scalar or a trivialization of $C_i$.

source.place: Local construction, last paragraph: normalize by the inverse automorphism at t=1

proof.text: Let $j:\mathbf G_{m,S}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_S$. The punctured product of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](3) gives $\kappa^\circ:j^*F\simeq j^*La^*C$. At $t=1$ it is $\theta$, because the product and fibre identifications are those of the same pair $(V,s)$. On $\mathbf G_{m,S_i}$, the maps $j^*\kappa_i$ and $\kappa^\circ$ agree at $1$ by Step 4. By Step 3 they are maps of finite locally constant sheaves with a common shift. The second assertion of [lem-pur-lisse-uniqueness] makes them equal on $\mathbf G_{m,S_i}$. On an overlap $S_{ij}$ the two normalized local comparisons therefore agree on its punctured line. The first assertion of [lem-pur-lisse-uniqueness] makes them agree on all of $\mathbf A^1_{S_{ij}}$. This is exactly the punctured-comparison and rigidity argument in the unit; it does not use descent of arbitrary local systems along the affine line.

source.place: Gluing: agreement on the punctured family and then on overlaps (unit Steps 2-3)

proof.text: For the etale cover of the base, its base-changed affine-line cover is a cover in the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1)-(3), the module sheaves on these cover members, with their constant coefficient rings, are precisely restrictions to the localized sites. Regard the maps of Step 5 as module-sheaf morphisms using Step 3. On the pro-etale covering $\{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}\to\mathbf A^1_S\}$, [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] glues them uniquely; it also glues their inverses since inverse maps agree wherever the original maps agree. The two composites are the identity, by the uniqueness part of that same sheaf-gluing statement applied to the local identities. Restore the common shift using [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to obtain an isomorphism $\kappa:F\simeq La^*C$, with $Li_1^*\kappa=\theta$. For any other normalized isomorphism, compare it with $\kappa$ on the punctured line: [lem-pur-lisse-uniqueness], second assertion, makes them equal there, and the first assertion makes them equal on the whole line. Thus the isomorphism is unique and independent of the charts and of $\alpha_i,\beta_i$.

source.place: Gluing: ordinary sheaf axiom, inverse maps, global normalization and uniqueness

proof.text: Pull back $\kappa$ along $i_0$. With the isomorphism $\eta$ from Step 1 and $Li_0^*La^*C\simeq C$, this gives $q=(Li_0^*\kappa)\circ\eta^{-1}:Lz^*\omega_\pi\simeq C$. Define the asserted map to be $q^{-1}$. Its direction is therefore $Ls^*\omega_g\to Lz^*\omega_\pi$, as required. In the standard coordinates, $F$ is $La^*C$ by the standard-pair assertion of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](4), and the identity is normalized at $1$. Step 6 forces $\kappa$ to be that identity, so the fibre map is also the identity on the standard section invariant.

source.place: Last paragraph: restriction at t=0 and inversion; standard-pair normalization

proof.text: Let $b:S'\to S$ be any $k$-morphism with $S'$ separated finite type, and let $\bar b:\mathbf A^1_{S'}\to\mathbf A^1_S$ be its base change. By [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](5) the pulled-back actual deformation, section and normal bundle are those of the pulled-back pair; by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](3) its two dualizing objects are the pullbacks of the original ones. Constant-coefficient pullback is a functor computed termwise by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], so $L\bar b^*\kappa$ is an isomorphism $F'\to La'^*C'$ whose restriction at $1$ is the pulled-back fibre identification $\theta'$. Step 6 over $S'$ says there is only one such normalized map. Hence $L\bar b^*\kappa=\kappa'$. Pulling this equality back along $i'_0$ and inverting shows that the fibre isomorphisms also agree. The same argument applies to etale localization. The geometry and dualizing statements used here allow arbitrary base change, so no flatness hypothesis on $b$ is introduced.

source.place: Statement, final paragraph: explicit uniqueness argument for arbitrary base change

split_report.summary: Made the implicit finite-coefficient and finite-type purity framework explicit, retaining Z/ell^n via E=Q_ell; wrote eight proof steps including regularity, source-etale dualizing comparison, concentration, normalization, punctured rigidity, ordinary sheaf gluing, restriction/inversion and arbitrary base change. Reused existing nodes throughout, and did not use general smooth orientation or SGA. The upstream theorem is sorry and omits uniqueness and base-change clauses, so is not an attachment. Second reading writes the flat associated-graded and Rees-algebra chart comparisons, including rank zero; no additional nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Current main-20261015 sk-thm-dnc opening paragraph is realized by Steps 1-3; Local construction by Steps 1-2 and 4; Gluing by Steps 5-6; final restriction and base-change clauses by Steps 7-8. The stored older unit Steps 1,2,3 are realized by Steps 1-3, Steps 4-5, and Steps 5-8 respectively.

tool_uses.why: Only the finite-level fact that Lambda(d) is a locally constant rank-one sheaf is used in Step 3; this is a coefficient tool and changes none of the DNC route.
Step 6 uses generic gluing of morphisms of two fixed module sheaves; this is the ordinary sheaf axiom required by the DNC unit, not a replacement for its geometry or normalization.
Generic properness of the blowup along a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal verifies the scheme domain of the DNC construction; no change to the DNC route.
Generic identification of the pro-etale site on a cover member with the localized site permits ordinary sheaf-morphism gluing, as required by the DNC unit.

Relative etale coordinates for a smooth map are used before constructing its section normal bundle, so regularity is not deduced from a geometry statement already assuming that bundle. This generic geometric tool is the coordinate route of the unit.
